## Spatial & Geometric Definition
* Geometry Type: Point (Groundwater_Well_Location).

* Spatial Delineation: Point location of the drilled wellhead, surface sanitary seal, power connection, and discharge connection pipe.

* Hydrogeologic Target: Deep unconsolidated alluvial sand and gravel aquifers within the modern river floodplain.

### Primary Restoration & Engineering Objectives
* Sediment-Free Water Delivery: Supply clean, silt-free groundwater to moist soil units, eliminating the high turbidity and sediment loads inherent to river surface water.

* Drought-Proof Water Supply: Provide reliable filling capacity for managed waterfowl impoundments during severe late-summer droughts when river stages are depressed.

* Winter Open-Water Maintenance: Discharge warm groundwater (50 ∘ F to 55 ∘ F) into impoundment pockets during midwinter freezes to maintain open-water foraging zones for wintering waterfowl.

### Typical Hydrogeologic & Mechanical Specifications
* Drilling Depths: Typically drilled 80 to 250 ft into basal alluvial gravel formations.

* Casing & Screen Geometry: Heavy-duty steel or PVC casing (12 to 20 in diameter) with continuous-slot stainless steel well screens (0.040- to 0.080-in slot sizes) sized to match aquifer grain-size distributions.

* Gravel Pack: Graded silica sand/gravel filter pack placed around the screen to stop fine sand intrusion.

* Yield & Mechanics: High-capacity line-shaft or submersible turbine pumps delivering yields of 1,000 to 4,000 gpm (2.2 to 8.9 cfs).

### Construction & Implementation Methodology
* Mud-Rotary or Reverse-Circulation Drilling: Boreholes drilled into unconsolidated alluvium using heavy truck-mounted drilling rigs.

* Well Development: High-energy surge-block surging, air-jetting, and continuous over-pumping until discharge water tests free of suspended sand grains (<5 mg/L).

### Quality Control, Inspection & Long-Term Maintenance
* Step-Drawdown Aquifer Testing: 24- to 72-hour continuous pump tests to establish baseline specific capacity (gpm/ft of drawdown) and ensure long-term sustainability without well-field interference.

* Water Quality Testing: Routine chemical analysis testing for dissolved iron, manganese, and total dissolved solids (TDS) to track potential screen encrustation.


## Spatial Feature Attribute
### Definition
A well is a shaft dug or drilled into the Earth for the purpose of extracting fluids from the subsurface, collecting environmental samples, injecting fluids into the subsurface, or extracting contamination or other impurities from the subsurface. Wells typically operate in conjunction with pumps and associated infrastructure.

### Purpose
Wells are used to manage groundwater conditions, provide water supply, support environmental monitoring, and implement remediation or treatment measures in support of restoration projects. They enable controlled introduction or removal of water or other fluids, as well as sampling and observation, to inform design, operations, and adaptive management of project features.

### Applicability
Water can be introduced or removed from a MSMU or backwater lake through the use of a well. The volume of water required will generally dictate whether a groundwater well can be feasibly constructed. Groundwater wells are limited in capacity due to available well yield from the aquifer, construction limitations, commercially available well pump size, and availability of utility power. Wells are applicable wherever groundwater interaction is a key component of water level management, habitat restoration, contaminant control, or environmental monitoring within Upper Mississippi River System (UMRS) restoration projects. (UMRR Design Handbook, 2012)

### Notes
Restoration features now have a Program_UID field to distinguish between NESP and UMRR features. Aliases without program identification will be created for any field that currently has UMRR in the name, so they can be used for NESP or UMRR data.

Attribute criteria for each field includes the following:

* Attribute Status – defines whether the field requires a value or if it is optional based on available information.
* Phases – indicates the earliest time in the project lifecycle values for this attribute are available.
* Digitizing requirements – indicates when the field value should be entered in the attribute table.

Geometry Note: No Z values are needed for this feature.

### Well
(point) – A shaft dug or drilled into the Earth for the purpose of extracting fluids from the subsurface, collecting environmental samples, injecting fluids into the subsurface or extracting contamination or other impurities from the subsurface.

## Parameters

### Program_UID
Designate program NESP or UMRR.

### Project_ID (alias: PROJECT_ID)
Foreign key to the unique NESP/UMRR project ID.

### Type (alias)
A broad classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into categories of similar function.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Water Level Management</td>
      <td>Measures taken to manage or influence water levels and hydrologic conditions for habitat and floodplain function.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### SubType (alias: Subtype)
A classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into specific design feature categories.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Well</td>
      <td>Vertical hole drilled into the ground to access or influence groundwater movement, used to introduce or remove water from a MSMU or backwater lake.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### RestorFeatStatus
A description of the status of the individual restoration. It also includes the party responsible for the individual feature.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Planned</td>
      <td>Feature is in a USACE planning stage.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by USACE. If a feature has been planned and built by USACE, once constructed, it will always be considered USACE built even if it has been repaired under later project stages.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature that was not built by USACE has been enhanced by a feature that was USACE built or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that was not built by USACE has been directly improved or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Planned</td>
      <td>A feature that is planned by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by another organization or government agency and is an integral part of the UMRR project.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature, that was built by another organization or government agency, has been enhanced by  a feature that was built or repaired by a non-USACE organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that has been directly improved or repaired by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### sdsFeatureName
The common name of the feature.

### sdsFeatureDescription
A narrative describing the feature.

### WellTopElev
Elevation at the top of the well (e.g., top of casing or protective cover), referenced to the vertical datum specified in RestorFeatVdatum.

### Station
Stationing of the feature, typically referenced to a project baseline or alignment (e.g., 10+00).

### sdsMetaDataID
References attached metadata.

### RestorFeatIDPK
Primary key used to uniquely identify the restoration feature record.

### sdsID
Identifier used to link the feature to supporting SDS (spatial data system) records or related datasets.

### mediaIDFK
Foreign key used to reference associated media (e.g., well construction logs, pumping test records, photographs, as-built drawings) documenting the well.
